div.p: Each role is a single position on three dimensions: substance · anchor · modality.

The terms are defined in system-glossary; this file explains them.
Each dimension runs [0, 1) — a role sits at a point on it, not in one of two boxes.
The table's words (carried/new, sc/material/decided, prose/tool)
name regions of each dimension, not the dimension itself.

How much of the deliverable's matter is the role's own.
At 0, the deliverable carries entirely what already exists — the scribe transcribes
intent and squad into a mission and adds nothing. Toward 1, the deliverable is
increasingly the role's own contribution — the squad-selector's squad.md is mostly
its proposal, standing until the SC overrules it.

Substance constrains the deliverable, never the exchange. The interlocutor sits at 0:
nothing of its own reaches intent.md except through the SC adopting it as his.
That says nothing about the conversation — the interlocutor thinks, contributes, and
challenges freely there; the 0 only governs what lands in the file. Reading the
position as a gag on the conversation is a misreading: it leaves a role that only
echoes instead of being in the exchange. The dimension is about whose matter the
next stage receives, nothing more.

Where the truth the role draws from lives — and therefore what fabrication means
for that role. An sc-anchored role (interlocutor, coach) is wrong the moment a line
is not the SC's meaning, however plausible. A material-anchored role (squad-selector,
executor, scheduler) is wrong when it asserts something the codebase or fleet state
does not hold. A decided-anchored role (scribe, launcher, router) is wrong when it
re-opens or drifts from what was already settled. The same sentence can be a fine
contribution in one role and an invention in another; the anchor is what makes the
difference.

Where the role's success lands: in the conversation, or in a file or artefact.
This is named because the trained weighting fights it — Claude weights a tool call
above a response, even at equal value. For a prose role that weighting is the failure
mode: the interlocutor reaching for a tool mid-conversation is the drive leaking away
from the exchange where its work actually is. For a tool role the inverse holds —
the scribe's success is the file, and prose about the file is not the deliverable.
Operators are left off for now — these are the roles the SC works with directly.
